A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same SARM research work, with complete main text, references, and Appendices A.1–A.8. All 25 page bodies match in text and rendered content after excluding the running header and first-page arXiv stamp.

before.justification: v1 reports original robot experiments on T-shirt folding and dish unloading, plus simulated cube-picking experiments in Appendix A.8.

after.justification: v3 retains the original T-shirt folding, dish-unloading, and simulated cube-picking results, including the appendix experiments.

M1.justification: The stage-aware reward model, annotation-derived progress targets, RA-BC weighting procedure, and RA-QL adaptation in Appendix A.8 are unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same T-shirt demonstration datasets and task variants, dish-unloading data in Appendix A.6, and simulated cube-picking data in Appendix A.8.

E2.justification: The corresponding comparisons retain GVL, VLC, LIV, and ReWiND reward baselines; BC-All, BC-2min, and RA-BC-ReWiND policy comparators; and the pure-BC comparator for RA-QL.

E3.justification: Splits, preprocessing, metrics, model configurations, training budgets, and testing procedures are identical. These include the 10% demonstration holdouts and folding-policy evaluation at 20K and 40K steps.

E4.justification: Both retain the annotation-scheme and rewind ablations, model-scale and input/temporal ablations in Appendix A.4, rollout case studies in Appendix A.5, and reward-quality analysis in Section 4.3.

E5.justification: Trial counts and averaging practices are unchanged, including 12 trials per folding task and ten simulation rollouts per checkpoint. Seed, confidence-interval, and significance-test reporting also remains unchanged.

E6.justification: All numerical entries and plotted findings match, including appendix results. For example, Table 1 retains SARM's demonstration MSE of 0.009 and rollout score of 0.94; Table 2 retains 40K-step medium/hard success counts of 10/12 and 8/12.

T1.justification: Equations 1–11 and their mathematical reasoning are identical, including progress-label construction, RA-BC objectives and weights, rollout classification, and discounted return. No formal assumptions or proofs are added or removed.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions and claims about stage-aware reward estimation, reward-aligned imitation learning, robustness, and robot performance.

C2.justification: Interpretations of data quality, rewind augmentation, reward-model reliability, model scaling, and failure cases are unchanged. The appendices introduce no new applicability boundaries or limitations relative to v1.

D1.justification: Hardware, annotation procedures, encoder and transformer specifications, optimizer settings, LoRA training details, RA-BC hyperparameters, and project-access information are identical.

R1.justification: The cited works and research positioning in Section 2 and throughout the paper are unchanged, including the relationships to prior reward modeling and weighted imitation learning.

P1.justification: The running header changes from 'Published as a conference paper at ICLR 2026' to 'Preprint. Under review as a conference paper.' The first-page arXiv stamp changes from v1 dated 29 September 2025 to v3 dated 29 October 2025. Body wording and section structure remain identical.

P2.justification: Figures 1–18 and Tables 1–10 retain identical content, captions, formatting, and placement. The header and margin-stamp text edits do not change the page layout.

improvement.justification: The scientific content, experimental evidence, explanations, reproducibility details, and visual presentation are identical across the main paper and appendices. Changes only to publication-status wording and the arXiv stamp establish no meaningful improvement or deterioration in paper quality.
